formula_summary.likelihood_sentence: Likelihood compounds conditional edge exploit probabilities (from CISA KEV, FIRST EPSS, credential exposure, and ML anomaly boost) along the highest-probability path found by Yen's top-k search, mapped onto a fixed log scale L_n = (log10(max(L, 10⁻⁶)) + 6) ÷ 6 so multi-hop differences remain visible without cross-asset distortion.
formula_summary.consequence_sentence: Consequence propagates outages across the physical service dependency DAG (applying edge failure delays once and taking max population served among lost services to prevent double-counting), combining safety severity (50%), population affected (30%), and outage duration (20%).
formula_summary.attack_graph_role: Attack Graph = How they get in (IT → DMZ → OT L3–L0 reachability, CVEs, credentials, and ATT&CK techniques).
formula_summary.dependency_graph_role: Dependency Graph = What breaks (OT controllers → substations, water pumping, chlorine dosing, hospital, and traffic cascades).

data_sources.description: Scenario parameter assumptions and justifications
data_sources.source: CISA KEV catalog, github.com/cisagov/kev-data (catalog version 2026.10.29); EPSS by FIRST; INL Consequence-driven Cyber-informed Engineering (CCE)

assumptions_table.justification: KEV listing means exploitation has been confirmed in the wild, so a reachable KEV CVE should never rank as unlikely because of a low EPSS. This matters most for water: of the KEV-listed CVEs that also have a CISA ICS advisory in the water sector, half have EPSS below 0.1 (median 0.09, 16 CVEs, a small sample). Across all ICS KEV entries EPSS is not lower than KEV overall (median 0.67 vs 0.57), so the floor is a water-sector correction, not a general ICS one. 0.5 treats a reachable KEV CVE as at least a coin flip.
assumptions_table.source: CISA KEV catalog (BOD 22-01): a CVE is only added with evidence of active exploitation. EPSS figures: CISA KEV v2026.10.29 joined with the jgamblin/KEV_EPSS mirror (30 Oct 2026). The 0.5 value itself is a design choice.

assumptions_table.justification: Default passwords are public and tried automatically by scanners and botnets; failure mostly comes from the device being changed or unreachable, not from difficulty.
assumptions_table.source: Joint advisory AA23-335A (Dec 2023): IRGC-affiliated actors compromised internet-exposed Unitronics PLCs, including at US water facilities, likely by exploiting poor password security such as default passwords. Supports "this happens in practice", not the 0.9 number.

assumptions_table.parameter: P(success) vs exposed remote access without MFA (RDP/VPN)
assumptions_table.justification: Needs a working credential (guessing, stuffing or a leaked password), so harder than defaults but realistic over time for an internet-facing service.
EPSS values differ by orders of magnitude, so a log scale keeps differences visible. The bounds are fixed, not taken from the current assets, so changing one asset never moves another asset's score.

An anomaly is a signal, not proof of compromise. A score of 1.0 closes 30% of the remaining gap to certainty (p' = p + (1 - p) × 0.3 × score), so the ML raises priority without overriding the vulnerability evidence.

assumptions_table.value: Entry: Internet only. Max 3 hops. Only uses edges whose best CVE is KEV-listed or has EPSS ≥ 0.1, or that are a default-credential weakness
assumptions_table.justification: Mass-scanning attackers go for exposed, known-exploited weaknesses and default passwords, and do not chain long paths into OT.
assumptions_table.source: Design choice, consistent with MITRE ATT&CK for ICS campaigns C0031 (Unitronics, 2023) and C0066 (U.S. water utilities, 2026), both listing T0883 Internet Accessible Device and T1694.001 Default Credentials

assumptions_table.value: Entry: Internet + vendor VPN. Max 8 hops. All edges
assumptions_table.justification: Patient, well-resourced actors chain through IT and DMZ into control layers and use third-party access.

assumptions_table.value: Entry: one corporate workstation. Holds valid domain credentials (credential edges inside IT = 1.0). Max 6 hops
assumptions_table.justification: Models an employee or a stolen employee account: no need to break in, only to move laterally.

assumptions_table.value: Safety severity 0.5, people affected 0.3, outage hours 0.2 (sum = 1)
assumptions_table.justification: Physical safety dominates in critical infrastructure; people affected comes next; duration matters but is partly captured by the other two.
assumptions_table.source: Consequence-first framing follows INL's Consequence-driven Cyber-informed Engineering (CCE). The weights themselves are a design choice.

assumptions_table.value: Severity ÷ 4; people affected ÷ 500,000 (city population); outage hours ÷ 72 (longest outage in the scenario); each capped at 1
assumptions_table.justification: Puts each component on 0–1 before weighting. People affected is the largest people_served among services lost, not the sum (see consequence_numbers.md, rule 4), so overlapping populations are not double-counted.
Standard OS/app patch plus a reboot, usually possible within the month.

assumptions_table.value: 8 engineer-hours, 4 h downtime; only in a maintenance window
assumptions_table.justification: Firmware updates on controllers need vendor validation, testing and a process shutdown, so they are deferred (patchable_now = false).
Rule change plus testing that operations traffic still flows; no process stop needed.
Quick to switch off; the cost is operational (vendor support must be re-arranged), noted in the UI rather than counted as downtime.
Enrolment and testing for the remote-access gateway users.
Detection, not prevention: raises confidence, does not lower likelihood.
Deliberately more conservative than vendor headline figures, because targeted attackers bypass MFA (push fatigue, session/token theft).
assumptions_table.source: Microsoft Security blog (Aug 2019) reported that accounts using MFA are over 99.9% less likely to be compromised; we use 90% to allow for targeted bypass. The 0.1 value is a design choice.

limitations.title: EPSS Meaning vs Breach Probability
limitations.description: EPSS is the probability that a CVE sees exploitation activity somewhere in the wild over the next 30 days — it is NOT the probability that our specific asset is breached. Vidura uses EPSS and CISA KEV as relative weights gated by network reachability and persona constraints.

limitations.title: Simulated Municipal Topology (Navanagar)
limitations.description: The 29-asset IT/DMZ/OT topology, firewall rules, and 500,000-resident service capacities represent a realistic but fictional Indian smart city (Navanagar). All scenario parameters are explicitly tagged 'Scenario assumption'.

limitations.title: No Ground Truth for Cyber-Physical Risk Scores
limitations.description: There is no empirical ground-truth dataset of city-wide cyber-physical breach frequencies. Accordingly, Vidura never claims an 'accuracy percentage' for risk scores; instead, we verify mathematical invariants, parameter sensitivity (Kendall's τ), CVSS divergence reasons, and held-out anomaly detection precision/recall.
